## Default register

| Choice | Current value | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ordinary RMSEA, CFI, TLI, SRMR points | Misspecification-robust policy composer | Adopted; evaluation pending | Component gates; this pilot only prices evaluation |
| Ordinary fit-index intervals | None | Open | Lab Wald candidates; registration pending |
| Evaluation design | Tier-1 basis, ML and MAR-FIML | Harness; criteria pending | Smoke and bounded pricing controls |

Which fit-index corrections and intervals should ordinary users receive? This
harness prepares the comparison. The full pricing pilot stopped before sampling because the mtmm9 MAR target failed
the library stationarity verdict (Newton distance .01219143, budget .01). The
five-cell smoke passes; its one-draw timings cannot establish bias, coverage
or a preferred interval. Criteria and production authorization remain pending.

## Smoke timings

```{r}
path <- file.path("results", params$lane, params$run_id)
if (!file.exists(file.path(path, "cost.csv")))
  stop("Missing pricing results. Run scripts/run_pilot.sh, or select an existing run_id.")
cost <- read.csv(file.path(path, "cost.csv"))
checks <- read.csv(file.path(path, "generator_checks.csv"))
timing <- read.csv(file.path(path, "timing.csv"))
setup <- read.csv(file.path(path, "setup_timing.csv"))
priced <- aggregate(seconds ~ generator + estimator + N, cost, mean)
names(priced) <- c("Generator", "Estimator", "Sample size", "Mean seconds per draw")
priced[[4]] <- round(priced[[4]], 3)
knitr::kable(priced)
```

These are smoke timings, with one draw per cell, rather than a completed pricing
pilot. The intended pilot is blocked during population preparation. These costs
average only timing over the smoke models and misfit controls. The
full per-cell costs, setup timings, attempted denominators, availability and
failures are in this run's CSV files. Sampling costs include ordinary default
fitting, all point arms and all lab interval arms. Target calibration is a
separate one-time cost. Cached target timings repeat in cells sharing a target
and must not be summed as if they were independent work.

## Targets and conventions

The generating h1 population gains the catalog's omitted block. Every coefficient
in the block has the same standardized size: residual covariance divided by the
disturbance standard deviations, or loading/regression multiplied by the ratio
of predictor and outcome total standard deviations. The core supplies implied
moments; inadmissible generating populations fail before sampling. A cell may
specify the signed size directly or root-find the continuous population RMSEA
within absolute standardized size .4.

The RMSEA target is $\sqrt{G F_0/\mathrm{df}}$. Complete-data targets fit h1 and the independence baseline to population moments
with the library default fitter. RMSEA uses the number of groups; TLI uses nominal
degrees of freedom. Each MAR-FIML target uses one fixed 200,000-row draw with the
same generator and masking law as its cell. The saturated/user/baseline likelihood
contrasts are library components. This finite integration approximation has Monte
Carlo error; it is recorded with its seed and method, and is not an exact MAR
integral. Complete-data targets are retained beside estimator-specific targets.

The MAR law masks half of the variables independently conditional on one fully
observed cause. Its logistic slope is one after standardizing the cause, and the
intercept calibrates the expected rate in each draw and group. The configuration
can instead name the cause and targets. Fifteen percent means fifteen percent of
each target column, rather than fifteen percent of all entries.

Normal single-group data use the core model generator; grouped normal data use
Cholesky draws. Vale–Maurelli data use centered cubic Fleishman transforms and
inverted intermediate normal correlations. Independent-generator data apply a
covariance factor to independent Fleishman variables. The latter's configured
skewness and excess kurtosis describe the independent sources, not each observed
variable. Integer discretized scores use equal-probability thresholds with
Pearson-code correlation calibration. Their variances and means are the exact
score moments, so their own population targets are recomputed; a requested RMSEA
sizes the continuous parent, not the scored population. Every configured generator
must reproduce its own population covariance within 1% relative Frobenius error
in a separate million-row check. Infeasible calibrations fail without matrix repair.

Naive and lavaan-robust points use the lab compatibility composer (MLM for complete
ML, MLR for FIML). The ordinary `fit_measures()` supplies the adopted corrected
points. The lab supplies naive/scaled noncentral RMSEA intervals and both 90% Wald
variants. Noncentral CFI/TLI intervals and lavaan-robust SRMR are unavailable
components, retained with reasons. The square-root Wald variant can be unavailable
at zero corrected discrepancy. RMSEA lower bounds are clipped at zero and zero is
covered when that bound is zero. Conditional coverage, attempted-draw coverage,
availability and convergence are all retained per cell; no fit is discarded.

## Caveats

The planned pilot uses three models, two misfit controls, two sample sizes and normal/VM
data for ML and 15% MAR-FIML. Five draws per cell price the computation; they do
not estimate performance reliably. Smoke additionally exercises independent and
integer discretized generators. All tier-1 models are configurable. DWLS, richer
MAR, bootstrap comparators and a production grid await their own registration.

## Reproduce

From the repository root, using the read-only lane library:

```sh
R_LIBS=~/.cache/magmaan-rlib/lane-c Rscript experiments/decisions/09-fit-indices/run_experiment.R --help
R_LIBS=~/.cache/magmaan-rlib/lane-c nice -n 10 Rscript experiments/decisions/09-fit-indices/run_experiment.R --smoke --workers 2 --run-id fresh-smoke
experiments/decisions/09-fit-indices/scripts/run_pilot.sh fresh-pilot
quarto render experiments/decisions/09-fit-indices/report.qmd -P run_id:smoke-task145-final
```

Run within the repository's shared compute slice, with single-threaded BLAS/OpenMP.
Use fresh run IDs after changing source, configuration, libraries or seed base.
Matching runs resume per-draw checkpoints; changing the filter or worker count
preserves seeds. `R/config.R` is the pricing configuration; a CSV with those same
columns may be supplied with `--config`. Reports read only the selected local
result directory and never launch estimation.
